summary: Honduras admits US, EU, Canadian and most Western-hemisphere passports visa-free for 90 days under the CA-4 scheme shared with Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua; an online immigration pre-check can be completed before arrival. Other nationalities need a consular visa, some with prior "consulted" clearance.

conditionalWaivers.text: A US, Canadian or Schengen visa with at least six months of validity left lets travelers who would otherwise need a Honduran visa enter without one, for up to 90 days in the CA-4 area. Nationalities on Honduras's restricted list may still need prior approval, so confirm with the Instituto Nacional de Migración before booking.

fee.notes: USD 30 for a single-entry visa (30 days); a multiple-entry visa (90 days) costs USD 60, according to the National Institute of Migration and the Honduran Embassy in London. Fees may vary by consulate.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only for travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission (parts of South America and Africa). Not needed on direct arrivals from North America or Europe.

source.name: Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM), Honduras — Visas

declarations.name: Online immigration pre-check (Prechequeo Migratorio)
declarations.text: Honduras's National Migration Institute runs an online immigration pre-check (prechequeo) for both entry and exit at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn: you request a one-time token by email, submit your details for approval, and can download the approved pre-check to show the immigration officer. The portal takes no payment. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

source.name: Instituto Nacional de Migración (Honduras) — Prechequeo Migratorio portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash over USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China, consular service — Honduras destination guide

notes: Taking coral, shells or other marine products from the Bay Islands is prohibited.
Pre-Columbian artefacts may not be exported.

payments.text: Cards work in malls, hotels and across tourist-oriented Roatán, but mainland Honduras is cash-first. Carry lempiras in small notes. US dollars are widely accepted on the Bay Islands and can be exchanged everywhere, usually at unfavourable rates.

safety.text: Honduras has high rates of violent crime, but the places tourists actually go — the Bay Islands, Copán Ruinas, La Ceiba's beach resorts — are markedly calmer than the big cities. Use radio taxis or hotel transport in Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula, don't display valuables, and avoid road travel after dark.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Honduras travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the driest window on the mainland — ideal for Copán and hiking. The Bay Islands dive year-round, with the heaviest rain from about October to January and whale-shark season around Utila peaking in spring.

idp.text: Honduras is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Honduras is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Honduras yet.

tips.text: You can complete the online prechequeo at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before you fly, for arrival and again for departure, and download the approved pre-check to show the immigration officer. Whether it is mandatory is not officially stated.

Honduras shares one 90-day stay with Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua (the CA-4). Crossing between the four does not reset your clock — extend at a migration office or leave the zone (Belize, Costa Rica or Mexico) before day 90.
Roatán and Utila are among the cheapest places in the world to learn to dive. Book insurance that covers diving — Roatán has a hyperbaric chamber, but treatment is expensive without cover.
Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula have serious street crime. Use radio taxis or app rides rather than hailing cabs, avoid public buses, and don't walk with phones or jewellery on show.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Honduras?
faq.answer: Most Western travelers do not: the US, EU, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and most of the Americas enter visa-free for up to 90 days under the CA-4 scheme. Other nationalities need a consular visa, and some require prior "consulted" clearance from the National Institute of Migration.

faq.question: What is the Honduras prechequeo form?
faq.answer: An online immigration pre-check run by Honduras's National Migration Institute at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn, for entry or exit. You request a one-time token by email, submit your details for approval and can download the result to show the immigration officer; the portal takes no payment. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 90-day rule work in Honduras?
faq.answer: Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua share one migration zone: a single 90-day stay covers all four countries, and moving between them does not reset it. For longer stays, request an extension at a migration office or leave the zone — Belize, Costa Rica and Mexico are all outside it.

faq.question: Is Honduras safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The headline crime statistics are among the region's worst, but they are concentrated in the big cities — the Bay Islands and Copán see steady tourism with mostly petty incidents. Fly or use tourist shuttles between destinations, avoid night road travel, and use radio taxis in cities.

faq.question: Can I pay in US dollars on Roatán?
faq.answer: Usually yes. The Bay Islands price much of their tourism in US dollars and accept them readily, though change often comes in lempiras. On the mainland, stick to lempiras in cash outside hotels and malls.
